title: A context is a product area

statements.says: The repository holds two contexts: Studio, the app, and Architecture, the check that holds the shape of the code.
CONTEXT-MAP.md names the contexts and the paths each owns.
A word is banned only inside the context that claims the file.
A context is a product area, and the sign that something is a different product area is that a word has to mean two things.
Neither the size of the repository nor whether it splits by project or by folder is the test of a context.
The word check reads CONTEXT-MAP.md and keys its banned-word lists by context.
A file no context claims is judged by no list, and a path two contexts claim is a breach.
The catalogue is written into the map as the next context, and gets its own glossary the day Author or Publish writes code.
Slice joins Studio's banned words only once the activity strip stops spelling it.
Studio spends the word slice on a Part of a run and on a block of hours in the activity strip, while the code's shape needs the same word, and no single glossary can hold both.
Because a path two contexts claim is a breach, the map cannot drift away from the tree.
The map stops two glossaries being a burden, because it says which one applies where, in one screen.

One glossary with one winner was rejected, because it would ban the word the architecture needs to keep a word Studio spends on two small things, and would keep doing so every time an area grew a language.
A context per deployable was rejected, because Studio is one deployable and the check is a library nothing ships, so the count would be one and the two languages would still fight.
Splitting the catalogue out now as a third context was rejected for now, because it has almost no code of its own here and a context with no code gives the check nothing to judge.
